title: A captured window's shadow is much lighter, and can be adjusted
goal: A window captured by clicking it keeps a shadow, but today it is macOS's own shadow baked into the picture, which reads far too dark (especially on the dark canvas and when pasted into other apps). It should be noticeably more transparent by default and adjustable afterwards like any other shadow.
notes:
User's words (2026-10-13): "you added a large dropshadow. i don't mind the shadow but it's TOO dark. should be quite a bit more transparent." Screenshot 2026-10-12 18.39.57: a captured Photonz window on the dark canvas with a wide, very dark shadow around it.

From code reading (not run): window captures keep macOS's real shadow: ScreenCapturer.swift:109 config.ignoreShadows = false and :147 ignoreShadows = !includeShadow; RectSelection.swift:173-176 tries .withShadow then .bareBounds (WindowShot styles); preference Experiments.windowCaptureIncludesShadow (CaptureCenter.swift:256, :305). The shadow is baked pixels, so it cannot be lightened afterwards today. Architecture rule (CLAUDE.md): layer styling such as shadow is non-destructive, applied at render time, never baked into pixels. Layer shadow controls exist (shadowOpacity etc., PhotonzCore/LayerMotion.swift).
acceptance: Reproduce first: capture a window by clicking it (light and dark windows, over light and dark desktops); measure the shadow's darkest alpha and its reach in the captured PNG and on the canvas; record in the audit

Window captures keep the window's true shape (rounded corners, exact edges) but the shadow is no longer baked in: the capture is the bare window and the shadow is a non-destructive layer shadow (Layer styling, applied at render time) that matches macOS's shadow geometry (offset, blur, spread) at a much lighter default, roughly 40% of macOS's opacity, chosen by comparing side by side and written with numbers in the audit

The shadow is editable in the layer's shadow controls (opacity, blur, distance, colour) and can be switched off; the existing 'include shadow' capture preference still decides whether a shadow is added at all
Copy, drag-out, paste into other apps and export include the lighter shadow, with transparent pixels around it (not a dark box), MEASURED alpha at three points of the shadow
The capture's canvas size leaves room for the shadow's reach so it is never clipped
Captures made before this keep their baked shadow (no change to old images)
A walk or drill captures a window, checks the layer has a shadow style at the new default and that the bare image has no shadow pixels beyond its edge
Audit under queue/audits/; anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar (queue/bin/follow-up-bar.md), and written into this task's log if it does not.

log.note: Epic capture-clickthrough is staged later, but this is the user's own report (p1, source user), so it is worked rather than dropped.

Reproduced with the new probe drill --window-shot-diag on real titled windows (2x). macOS shadow fits a blurred offset box to within 0.6 alpha levels: inactive blur 11.75pt / 8pt down / opacity 0.25 light, 0.43 dark; active blur 19.5pt / 18pt down / 0.39 light, 0.68 dark; plus a 1px black hairline (0.2-0.95). The user's dark active window is the 0.68 case.

Built: window clicks are shot bare; macOS's shadowed shot is read for shape and darkness (WindowShot.readSystemShadow, PhotonzCore) and the window gets [soft, hairline] drop shadows at 40% as a layer style (WindowShot.document). WindowCaptureShadow (PhotonzRender) flattens it in the window's own colour space (P3 kept) and takes the window pixels out of the shadowed shot masked by the bare alpha, because the bare shot loses a dark window's light 2px rim. CaptureStore.add writes the PNG then the .photonz sidecar, so history copy/drag/paste get the lighter shadow and editing reopens the layer.

Verified: 20 unit tests (measured profiles as fixtures, three-point alpha at 40%, transparent corners, rim kept, P3 kept); drill PASS on inactive and active light/dark windows (alpha below active dark: 134/54, 81/32, 24/9); walk a-captured-window-s-shadow-is-light-and-editable-walk green at Next defaults (Window layer unlocked, Shadow 1 opacity 27%, switch off/on). Full suite 12853 tests green.

left rough (not filed, below the bar until the user answers the audit question): switching the whole shadow off is two clicks because the hairline is its own Shadow 2; panel shows shadow numbers in image px like every capture; edge line set in px from the 2x measurement, untested at 1x.

Window clicks are shot bare and given macOS's own shadow shape at 40% of the darkness macOS drew, read per window, as a layer style on an unlocked Window layer. The PNG is flattened from it (transparent around, Display P3 kept, dark window rim kept) and a .photonz sidecar beside it makes the shadow editable and switchable on edit. Verified: 20 unit tests, probe drill PASS on inactive/active light/dark windows (three-point alpha ours vs macOS 54/134, 32/81, 9/24), walk a-captured-window-s-shadow-is-light-and-editable-walk green at Next defaults, full suite green.
